core_claim: Zurich's exploding-snowman folk forecast does not predict summer temperature - the correlation is non-significant and points the wrong way - while the same 67-year record shows real, accelerating warming on the Swiss Plateau.

edt_01.label: The snowman gets a microphone
edt_01.title: The snowman gets a microphone
edt_01.editorial_notes: Hook with 2023's 57-min burn followed by 20.07C summer. Embed the Boeoegg burning video (inst_01). Hook should land before any prose explaining what the festival is.

edt_02.label: The folk rule, in one chart
edt_02.title: The folk rule, in one chart
edt_02.editorial_notes: r=0.194 and p=0.121 are exact, do not round. Highlight that correlation is the wrong direction. The scatter is the centerpiece chart of the whole blog.

edt_03.label: How wrong, exactly
edt_03.title: How wrong, exactly
edt_03.editorial_notes: Best place for a guess-first interaction: ask the reader to predict whether fast burns are followed by hotter summers. Then reveal the 41.5% vs 84.6% comparison. Numbers 6.3% / 24.2% / 41.5% / 84.6% must be exact.

edt_04.label: But the burns themselves keep getting weirder
edt_04.title: But the burns themselves keep getting weirder
edt_04.editorial_notes: Decadal mean duration chart - 2020s averaging 33.6 min stands out. Tie the swings to MeteoSwiss's pyre / humidity / accelerant explanation.

edt_05.label: And the summers really are getting hotter
edt_05.title: And the summers really are getting hotter
edt_05.editorial_notes: 1.86C, 4.15C, 66.7% are exact numbers. The visual centerpiece here should let the reader see the trend (line of best fit + record-summer markers). Do NOT frame this as a hidden snowman skill - it is the snowman's blind spot.

edt_06.label: What we keep watching
edt_06.title: What we keep watching
edt_06.editorial_notes: Closing beat that explains the 2020/2024 NAs and ends on an open question. Embed inst_02 (DW Euromaxx explainer) for non-Swiss readers who want the festival itself, or repeat inst_01. Avoid summary - end on tension.
